title: Read-it-later app Pocket shut down — here are the best alternatives

body:
Pocket, the popular read-it-later application, is set to shut down on October 8, 2025, leaving users with a limited timeframe to export their saved content. This decision has prompted discussions about the future of personal content management and the alternatives available for users who rely on the app to save articles and other online content for later reading.

What happened

Pocket has announced its impending shutdown, giving users until October 8, 2025, to export their saved articles and other important items. This includes a variety of content such as lists, archives, favorites, notes, and highlights that users have accumulated over time. The announcement has raised concerns among users who have come to depend on Pocket for managing their reading materials and online resources.

Why it matters

The closure of Pocket signifies a significant shift in the landscape of content management applications. For many users, Pocket has been an essential tool for curating and organizing online content, allowing them to save articles from various sources and access them at their convenience. The shutdown not only affects individual users but also highlights the challenges faced by digital platforms in maintaining user engagement and sustainability in an ever-evolving tech environment.

As users prepare for the transition, they are encouraged to explore alternative applications that offer similar functionalities. The closure of Pocket serves as a reminder of the importance of data portability and the need for users to have control over their saved content. With the deadline approaching, users must act quickly to ensure they do not lose their valuable saved articles and resources.

Source: techcrunch.com.
